reasons: The rule is a 'missing'-kind insert and the rationale credibly surveys the candidate clauses (Sections 4, 8(b), 14, 16, 17, 18) showing exit obligations run only against us (cease use, certify destruction of Software) with no reciprocal data-return, transition-assistance or deletion-certification mechanic, so neither the preferred nor the fallback position is met.

The inserted Section 17(d) tracks the playbook model language closely (up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, return of data within thirty days in a machine-readable format, then deletion with written certification) and is placed at the end of the Term and Termination section, which is the location the redline guidance specifies; subsection lettering (d) follows the existing (b)/(c) sequence.

The insert is additive only — no existing text is altered or deleted — so the edit is the smallest change that reaches the playbook position; the modest extension to Confidential Information alongside data is consistent with the rule's intent and does not create a directional problem for us.

Comment is accurate (correctly characterises the one-sided Section 17(b) obligation), concise, in first person plural with the required prefix, states the playbook position and offers the 90-day fallback, matching tone requirements.
Deterministic checks both pass and are consistent with the substance of the insert.
